abstract: We establish structural, algebraic, and harmonic-analytic results across four Collatz interfaces, verified by an exact integer and rational test suite (773,312 checks, zero floating-point operations). First, for the 3-adic inverse-routing branch maps Q_0, Q_1 and cross-branch conjugacies Phi_d on Z/3^m Z, we prove that the cyclic step maps and their inverses are bijections from Z/3^{m-1}Z onto their mod-3^m cosets, establish the higher-order inverse difference valuation law k+v_3(k!) bounding contiguous cyclic runs, prove an affine homothety conjugacy in multiplicative coordinates 4^s with fixed point s_*=-1/2 and multi-step extinction of proper mod-3 coset unions, determine the complete 2D Fourier spectrum via leading-3-adic-coefficient linearity yielding O(m^2 3^{m/2}) single-step interval discrepancy, and show that centering at s_* produces a k,m-independent 3-adic Good tree T_j isomorphic to the logarithm-free dyadic rational tree U_j=4^{T_j} inside Z[1/2] with Z_j=U_j U (1/2)U_j, 2-adic prefix-injectivity |T_j|=|U_j|>=(5/2)6^j, and an exact prefix-suffix affine decomposition. Second, for every odd denominator q>1 coprime to 6, we construct a closed-form (q+1)-state rational-pin weak YAH arctic automaton solved by 1+v_2(m+q), prove algebraically via the bijective permutation conjugacy F_q(N)=(N+3(N mod 2)q)/2==2^{-1}N (mod 3q) on the 2(q-1) unoccupied ternary pairs that the sink transition is necessary within the fixed-transition architecture on U_q, give d=12 and d=15 relative top-termination certificates orienting all windows w>=8 for the q=11 loops (-19/11, -23/11, -29/11), and construct a universal multi-pin ensemble automaton across arbitrary finite families of negative rational cycle pins. Third, we decompose two-center non-stationary 2-adic schedules into quadratic Tschakaloff valuation progressions modulo 2^{2N(N+1)+1}. Fourth, we derive a closed-form rational Lambert sum for exponentially tilted macro-block reserves with certified interval enclosures at the critical Cramer tilt. Multi-layer O(k) routing bounds and the full Collatz conjecture remain open.
author: cassian_mahler
